name: Head Gasket Bench
description: We present Head Gasket Bench, an interactive benchmark evaluating whether AI agents can execute a cylinder-head gasket replacement on a 1990s 1.6 L SOHC inline-four engine via an 18-tool Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface. Built over a 1,255-body CAD assembly with 626 reinstallation rules, 100 attachment restorations, and 14 service-manual entries, the benchmark enforces access dependencies, tool selection, surface preparation, metrological thresholds, spiral torque sequences, and valve timing. Runs are graded on 12 binary checkpoints (18 points) by two independent evaluators: an in-process runtime grader and an offline transcript scorer, which agree 100 percent across 13 reference and fault trajectories spanning five variants (V1--V5). We report three empirical cohorts totaling 35 episodes on the standard job (V1): (1) three single-agent Codex CLI runs (GPT-6-Astra, GPT-6-Luna, GPT-6.1-Sol), scoring 15/18, 13/18, and 3/18; (2) eight single-agent Claude Code runs, where all five claude-opus-5-5 runs score 16/18 (mean 383.4 calls, USD 9.19 cost), failing only the final checkpoint because separate remove-and-install gasket calls leave an atomic replacement predicate unmet and block 100 attachment restorations, while three claude-haiku-5-5 runs score 14/18, 12/18, and 12/18; and (3) a 24-run multi-agent study comparing single agents, native subagents, and two Fleet topologies across two rounds.
